Let x be the masked context, y the target, A(x,y) the eligible negative items, and m_j their sampled multiplicities. With uncorrected logits, training minimizes the expected sampled-candidate cross-entropy E[log(e^{s_y}+Σ_{j∈A}m_j e^{s_j})−s_y], over training examples and K replacement draws. This is a contrastive classification objective, generally different from full-catalog likelihood. Duplicates count repeatedly: multiplicity m_j is equivalent to adding log(m_j) to that negative’s logit; deduplication changes the objective. These conclusions follow directly from the denominator and agree with the replacement-sampling formulation in [Blanc & Rendle (2018)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a/blanc18a.pdf).

Importance-corrected sampled softmax keeps the deterministic positive unchanged and subtracts log(Kq(j|x,y)) from each sampled negative. For uniform eligible sampling, q=1/|A|, giving partition estimate e^{s_y}+(|A|/K)Σ_j m_j e^{s_j}. This partition estimate is unbiased for {y}∪A, but its logged loss and normalized gradient are generally biased at finite K; they converge to that restricted softmax as K grows. Without correction, increasing K does not recover this normalization. Applied to the proposed sampler, history exclusion gives omitted catalog items zero proposal probability: importance weighting cannot recover their contributions. Target-dependent eligibility therefore requires the actual conditional proposal and generally defines different candidate universes across targets; full-catalog consistency requires restoring missing support or explicitly accounting for omitted terms.

[Khrylchenko et al., “Correcting the LogQ Correction” (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.09331v2) explicitly separates the always-present positive from sampled negatives. Its reformulation uses negative-only importance normalization and a stop-gradient weight estimating 1−P(y|x). It addresses deterministic-positive treatment, not arbitrary history exclusions, and does not establish finite-K unbiasedness for this sampler. Its full-catalog derivation requires proposal support over every non-target item.
